# Breaking spec changes that were made deliberately. One per line.
#
# FORMAT: oasdiff lowercases each change's single-line rendering (`oasdiff breaking -f singleline`)
# and ignores it if any line here appears in it as a substring. So a line must be the *lowercased*
# message with the leading `error at <spec path>, ` stripped — the path differs between a local run
# and CI, and including it would silently stop the entry matching. Comment lines never match
# anything, which is why they are safe here.
#
# WHY THIS FILE IS SHORT: the gate exists because the SPA is deployed separately from the API, so a
# version skew window always exists and a breaking change ships silently as a runtime
# deserialisation failure in the browser. An entry is therefore a claim that the *only* consumer of
# that operation is `web/frontend`, and that it was updated in the same commit. Anything a caller
# outside this repository could hit does not belong here — it gets a new endpoint and a deprecation
# instead, the way `/v1/admin/scans/stream` did.
#
# Keep each entry pinned to the exact operation and the exact from/to shape, so this file cannot
# quietly absolve a *different* break on the same endpoint later.

# The audit trail and the scan history were fixed-size unfiltered feeds that fall off the end
# under load. Paging them needs a total, a pager cannot say
# "1-40 of N" without one, and a total cannot ride alongside a bare array — so both responses
# became `{ items, total }`. Consumed only by the operator console.
in api get /v1/admin/audit the response's body `type` changed from `array<object>` to `object` for status `200`
in api get /v1/admin/scans the response's body `type` changed from `array<object>` to `object` for status `200`

# The rebuild endpoint used to await the whole build inside the request handler, which meant the
# control plane's 30 s request timeout decided how long a build was allowed to take: it dropped the
# handler future mid-run, the claim was never released, and every later build declined to start.
# The build now runs detached, so the response can only report whether one was *started* — these
# three counts are not knowable when it answers, and are read from
# `GET /v1/admin/recommendations/health` instead. Consumed only by the operator console, which
# already ignores this response body and polls that endpoint.
in api post /v1/admin/recommendations/rebuild removed the required property `series_built` from the response with the `200` status
in api post /v1/admin/recommendations/rebuild removed the required property `vocabulary` from the response with the `200` status
in api post /v1/admin/recommendations/rebuild removed the required property `dense_dims` from the response with the `200` status

# The notification preferences were an unvalidated free-form document — and nothing on the server
# ever read it, so the three toggles the account panel wrote had no effect on delivery at all. They
# are a typed, versioned contract now, which is what makes a saved preference one the notifier
# honours. Every field defaults, so the widest previously-valid body an old bundle could send —
# `{}` — is still accepted and still means "the product defaults"; what this break rejects is a
# body that was never a preference document, such as a bare string or array. Consumed only by
# `web/frontend`, updated in the same commit.
in api put /v1/me/notification-prefs the request's body `type` changed from `any` to `object`

# Two-factor authentication. `POST /v1/auth/login` used to answer with a session unconditionally;
# it now answers `{ status, session?, mfa? }`, because an account holding a second factor must come
# away from the password leg with *no* session at all — a token issued beside the challenge would
# leave the password a complete credential for anyone who skipped the prompt. `TokenResponse`
# itself is untouched, so `/v1/auth/refresh` and `/v1/auth/register` keep the shape they had, and
# the three properties below moved into `session` rather than disappearing. Consumed only by
# `web/frontend`, updated in the same commit.
in api post /v1/auth/login removed the required property `access_token` from the response with the `200` status
in api post /v1/auth/login removed the required property `token_type` from the response with the `200` status
in api post /v1/auth/login removed the required property `expires_in` from the response with the `200` status

# `manga_themesia` was never a value this API accepted. `AdapterKind` publishes one token per
# variant and the schema derive did not read the per-variant `#[serde(rename)]`, so the document
# carried the container's `rename_all` applied to the identifier while the database, the handlers
# and every response said `mangathemesia`. Removing it takes away a value that could only ever
# have produced a 422, and the drift is what broke the console: a client generated from the
# document refused every provider list carrying such a provider. Pinned by
# `tankovault_domain::enums`' `the_published_vocabulary_is_the_one_serde_writes`.
in api post /v1/admin/providers removed the enum value `manga_themesia` of the request property `adapter`
